name: unity-dev
description: Unity 6 game development, twenty-nine load-by-situation skills covering the whole loop from an empty project to a verified artifact. Terminal & verification: unity-cli (the CLI's surface, exit codes that say whether a retry is honest, MCP wiring, the warm shell), unity-debug (CHECK THE INSTRUMENT FIRST — stale results files and settings assets that were never in effect; four loops, the fastest driving a LIVE Editor in sub-second round trips against ~20 s for batchmode; Safe Mode's deadlock). Day one: unity-new-project (editor pinning, .meta/LFS, UPM deps pinned to annotated tags, IL2CPP/ARM64, asmdef boundaries, and the async/-quit deadlock that makes a headless package install exit 0 and install nothing). UI: unity-game-ui (detects the project's UI system and routes; owns the runtime IMGUI HUD that editor-tooling docs never cover — GUI.matrix scaling, event swallowing, a type scale derived from viewing distance in arcminutes, mixed Latin/CJK font authoring), unity-ui-ugui (the six ways Canvas UI renders nothing, and the Layout Group vs ContentSizeFitter conflict), unity-ui-toolkit (USS is a subset of CSS and an unsupported property is ignored, not an error). Assets: unity-3d-models (decimate AI-generated GLB before Unity sees it), unity-2d-sprites (sprite metadata lives in the importer; a set of frames turned into a playable AnimationClip; the capability gate that prevents silent corruption), unity-rigged-character (characters take the FBX route because glTFast cannot build an Avatar; bind-pose bounds make measured hitboxes arm-span wide), unity-2d-pixel-perfect (soft, crawling or seam-ridden pixel art, across both of the components called PixelPerfectCamera), unity-sprite-atlas (V2 atlases from script: the editor/runtime split, packing and platform settings, and how the packed texture reaches the player), unity-tilemap (Tile Palettes for rectangular, hexagonal and isometric grids, and RuleTiles generated from a terrain sheet you already have). Runtime domains: unity-physics-3d (symptom-routed triage, first-match-wins, a two-sided probe), unity-navigation (the agent owns the transform — decide that first), unity-render-urp (the Volume pre-flight behind 'I set it and nothing happened', the mobile subset, an eight-point Render Graph review), unity-audio (load types, sample rates, mixer cost; reports before it reimports), unity-localization (the CJK font pipeline, and the two contradictory standard answers for it). Shipping: unity-android-release (build it then PROVE it — a driver that refuses rather than warns, reading the artifact back with aapt/apksigner, per-build provenance), unity-web-release (the server headers that undo every Unity setting, and iOS Safari's memory ceiling). Backend & commerce: unity-live-services, unity-monetization, unity-multiplayer, and the API layer they hand off to — unity-ugs (which package provides what, the initialisation order everything else depends on, Cloud Save access classes, Cloud Code, Remote Config, the Deployment Window file types), unity-iap (In-App Purchasing v5 call by call: store connection, the pending/confirm flow, receipts, entitlement, restore), unity-ads-levelplay (LevelPlay mediation: native dependency resolution, consent before init, rewarded/interstitial/banner units, impression-level revenue), unity-multiplayer-services (the Sessions API: join codes, a browsable game list, quick join, ticket matchmaking, relay, host migration, dedicated servers), unity-vivox (voice and text chat: sign-in, group/echo/positional channels, the roster, mute and push-to-talk, microphone permission). AI asset generation: codex-visual (2D art through the codex image model, held on-style by one art bible and one anchor — grid one-shot sets, animation sheets generated as one grid and sliced into measured frames with a GIF preview, chroma-key transparency, normalised sizes), comfyui-asset-generation (music, SFX and MiniMax H3 video through a self-hosted ComfyUI — one job at a time, /history as the only proof, /free before a model switch). Install in Unity projects.
